newsitem.title: FRANCE: Protesters attack French far-right book stand.
newsitem.headline: Protesters attack French far-right book stand.

text.p: Unidentified protesters ransacked a book stall displaying literature by France's extreme-right National Front party at the Paris Book Fair on Thursday, police said.
A police spokeswoman said about 20 people were involved in the attack. No one immediately claimed responsibility and there were no arrests.
Sophie Brissaud, a spokeswoman for the anti-immigration party's leader Jean-Marie Le Pen, told Reuters: "Our representatives were attacked. The stand was ransacked."
In a statement, the party called the attack "deliberate and scandalous" and said it had caused unspecified injuries.
The annual book fair, one of Europe's biggest, opened on Wednesday and runs until March 17.

The newspaper Le Monde reported that other publishers exhibiting at the show had circulated petitions protesting against the presence of the National Front's booth, but stopped short of calling for it to be shut down.
The ransacked booth was displaying books and pamphlets written by National Front party leaders and supporters.
